publications.name: The lambda number of the power graph of a finite p-group
publications.summary: An L(2, 1)-labelling of a finite graph is a function that assigns integer values to the vertices V(gamma)of gamma (colouring of V(gamma) by Z) so that the absolute difference of two such values is at least 2 for adjacent vertices and is at least 1 for vertices, which are precisely distance 2 apart. The lambda number lambda(gamma) of gamma measures the least number of integers needed for such a labelling (colouring). A power graph of a finite group G is a graph with vertex set as the elements of G and two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if one of them is a positive integer power of the other. It is known that for any finite group. In this paper, we show that if G is a finite group of a prime power order, then lambda(gamma_G) = |G| if and only if G is neither cyclic nor a generalized quaternion 2-group. This settles a partial classification of finite groups achieving the lower bound of lambda number.
